annotations.title: Check a price before you pay

description: Use this before paying: when a user or agent has a proposed price for something (a rent, a home, a litre of fuel, a medicine, a contract) and wants to know whether it is typical against recorded official evidence. Give the category (broadband, cars, childcare, construction, contracts, diet-costs, energy, farm-gate-prices, farm-prices, flights, fuel, groceries, home-sales, home-upgrades, hotels, insurance, land-prices, medical, medicines, producer-prices, rent, tuition and wholesale-power), the country, the same parameters that category's own tool takes, and the price. It runs the category's normal answer and returns a verdict: within, above or below the typical range (10th–90th percentile of recorded prices) when the evidence is a set of records; about, above or below the average when the evidence is one official average or median (within 5% counts as about average, and it says plainly this is an average, not a distribution); or cannot_judge, with the reason, when the currency or unit differs (ProofPrice never converts), there are too few records or nothing matched. It also returns where the price sits (for example '27% above the median and above the 90th percentile'), the reasons and cautions (posted prices are not paid prices, old periods), what is missing, one quotable sentence, and the full evidence answer with source, licence and audit-trail fields to keep with the reasoning. Do not use it to value one specific item or address, as financial or legal advice, or to compare prices in different currencies or units.

name: pricepaid_check_price

outputSchema.description: A price check: a verdict on a proposed price against recorded evidence, where it sits, why, what is missing, and the full evidence answer. Deterministic: no benchmark is ever invented.

answer.description: The full evidence answer (the same answer the category tool returns), embedded so the reasoning can be kept with its source, licence and audit-trail fields.

answer_id.description: Audit trail: a stable id (hash of source id, normalised query, data period and method_version). The same question on the same data gives the same id; keep it with the reasoning that used the figure.

as_of.description: When the answer was produced (ISO 8601); the snapshot date when the official source was down and the answer comes from our copy.

data_age_days.description: Whole days between data_as_of and retrieved_at; null when data_as_of is null.

data_as_of.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the newest data point behind the figure; null when unknown.

evidence.description: Audit trail: what kind of evidence the figure is.

label.description: Short name of the kind of evidence, e.g. 'Recorded sale prices', 'Official published average', 'Posted shelf or pump price', 'Contract award value', 'Regulated reimbursement price'.

meaning.description: One sentence on what this kind of evidence does and does not establish.

extra.description: Source-specific details (for example cheapest stations). extra.stale is true when the answer comes from our copy of the source.

method_version.description: Audit trail: version of the way this source turns raw data into an answer (per source, default '1').

notice.description: Information, not a valuation or offer. Also says when the answer is our copy because the official source did not respond.

period.description: The period the records cover (ISO dates), or the date of the snapshot when the answer comes from our copy.

anyOf.description: The price. Null when there is not enough data to publish a figure (fewer than 5 records) or nothing matched.

measure.description: What value is: median for ranges built from records; average or median for official statistics.

typical_high.description: 90th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

typical_low.description: 10th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

unit.description: What the price is per, e.g. 'per litre', 'per home', 'per kWh'.

value.description: The headline figure. For ranges built from records it equals median.

price_type.description: transaction, posted_pump_price, posted_price, contract_price, reimbursement_price or official_statistic.

query.description: The request as understood, echoed back.

reliability.description: How far to trust the figure as a distribution of real prices. official_with_count = a published official figure with a record count; official_median_no_count = a published average or median with no record count (confidence 'high' there means the publisher is official, not that a count was checked); record_level = 15+ records we hold; thin = 5–14 records; stale = our copy because the official source did not respond; insufficient_data = no figure published.

retrieved_at.description: Audit trail: when ProofPrice produced this answer (ISO 8601). For an answer from our own copy this is now, while as_of is the snapshot date.

sample_size.description: Number of records behind the figure; null when the publisher does not say.

source.description: Where the figure comes from, under which licence, and the attribution line to show.

attribution.description: The attribution line to show with the figure.

url.description: The publisher's page for this data.

statistic.description: Official statistics only: what kind of figure it is and the period the publisher states it for.

status.description: ok = a figure is returned; insufficient_data = fewer than 5 matching records; no_matches = nothing matched.

suggestions.description: Short plain things to try next: widen the period or area, ask for an itemised quote. May be empty.

summary.description: One plain sentence an AI can quote.

input.description: The price check as understood, echoed back. currency and unit are null when not given (the evidence currency and unit were assumed).

missing.description: What stopped or limits the comparison (currency or unit mismatch, too few records, nothing matched). Empty when nothing is missing.

basis.description: range = records with a 10th–90th percentile; average = one published official figure, not a distribution.

reference_value.description: The median or published average the price is compared with.

text.description: Where the price sits, e.g. '27% above the median and above the 90th percentile'.

vs_median_percent.description: Percent difference from the median (range basis) or from the published figure (average basis); positive = above.

position.description: Where the price sits against the evidence; null when cannot_judge.

reasons.description: Why this verdict, including cautions (posted versus paid prices, old periods, assumptions made).

summary.description: One plain sentence an AI can quote.

verdict.description: within/above/below_typical_range: the price compared with the 10th–90th percentile of recorded prices. about_average/above_average/below_average: compared with one published official average or median (within ±5% = about_average). cannot_judge: the evidence cannot honestly be compared (see reasons and missing).

title: Check a price before you pay
